risk_signals: test asserts sample loss as expected outcome when isolation is disabled
units.reason: New test only; it cannot change production behavior, though it records known data loss when isolation is disabled.
units.headline: Test: late append during selected-series compaction survives restart
units.summary: Uses the before-evict hook to append a sample with t=400 after the block is written, then checks that the sample is still there before and after a WAL-replay restart. When isolation is disabled, the test expects the late sample to be lost permanently. Reviewers should know that this loss is accepted behavior; the test logic itself is simple.

units.reason: New test only; it covers an appender opened before compaction that commits inside the eviction window.
units.headline: Test: pre-opened appender committing mid-compaction keeps series in head
units.summary: Opens an appender before CompactSelectedSeries and commits it from the before-evict hook. It then checks that the series is not evicted and that all three samples survive a restart. It skips when isolation is disabled. It adds coverage and changes no production code.

units.reason: Small predicate (s.ooo == nil) pulled out as a helper and used by the stale and selected-series filters.
units.headline: Add isSeriesWithoutOOO predicate helper
units.summary: Adds a one-line helper that is true when a series has no out-of-order state. CompactSelectedSeries, staleSeriesRefsNoOOOData and both truncate paths use it. It is trivially equivalent to the inline nil check.

units.reason: Stale-NaN check moved out of gcStaleSeries into a helper with identical logic.
units.headline: Extract stale-NaN last-value check into isStaleSeries
units.summary: The float, histogram and float-histogram stale-NaN checks are the same as the removed inline code in gcStaleSeries. The helper is now used for filtering, eviction predicates and counting deleted stale series. Since the logic is unchanged, a line-by-line review is not needed.

units.reason: Changes which stale series are evicted and written as WAL tombstones; mistakes there lose data.
units.headline: truncateStaleSeries skips series with appendIDs above watermark
units.summary: Stale-series eviction now goes through the generic truncateSeries with a predicate: no OOO data, still stale, and no appendID above the watermark. The extra watermark guard keeps series that got samples after the block write began, so they are not tombstoned. Tests pass math.MaxUint64 to turn the guard off.
focus: Which value compactHeadViewLocked passes as appendIDWatermark (lastAppendID vs committedAppendID), and that it is captured before the block write
The guard is a no-op when isolation is disabled, so concurrent writes to stale series can still be lost
truncateSeries now evicts when MinTime == maxt (it used to return early)

issues.title: Doc says watermark is lastAppendID; test says that would be wrong
issues.evidence: // appendIDWatermark is the lastAppendID captured before the upstream block write.
issues.failure_scenario: An appender opened before compaction holds an appendID <= lastAppendID and commits during the write window. If the watermark really were lastAppendID, hasAppendIDAbove would return false and the late sample would be evicted and tombstoned. TestCompactSelectedSeries_OpenAppenderCommittingDuringCompaction says lastAppendID would wrongly cover it, so either this doc is out of date or the caller is wrong.
issues.detail: The doc comment disagrees with the PR's own test about what the watermark is; the caller in compactHeadViewLocked is not shown.

risk_signals: new eviction path for non-stale series
units.reason: New path that evicts and tombstones live non-stale series; a wrong predicate means permanent sample loss.
units.headline: New truncateSelectedSeries evicts chosen series without OOO data
units.summary: Evicts the given series when they have no OOO data and no appendID above the watermark, and writes WAL tombstones for them. Unlike the stale path, the series do not need to be stale, so with isolation disabled any concurrent append to a selected series is lost after eviction.
focus: The watermark must cover only appends that were committed before the block write (see the open-appender test)
With isolation disabled there is no guard; check that callers such as Mimir really guarantee no writes to these series
Samples with timestamp > maxt are protected only by gcSeries' maxTime check

issues.title: Doc says watermark is lastAppendID, contradicting open-appender test
issues.evidence: // appendIDWatermark is the lastAppendID captured before the upstream block write.
issues.failure_scenario: An appender opened before CompactSelectedSeries commits in the before-evict window. With a lastAppendID watermark its ID is not above it, so the series would be evicted and the t=400 sample lost. The PR's test says lastAppendID would be incorrect, so the comment misdescribes the contract.
issues.detail: Either the comment is out of date (likely committedAppendID is used) or the caller uses the wrong watermark; the caller is not shown.

units.reason: Core guard that decides whether compaction may evict a series that has received concurrent writes.
units.headline: Add hasAppendIDAbove to detect post-watermark appends via txRing
units.summary: Walks the series' txRing of uncleaned append IDs and reports whether any is greater than the watermark; returns false when txs is nil (isolation disabled). The ring always keeps the newest append's ID, so a post-watermark append stays detectable. The claim about disabled isolation matches the code.
focus: Callers must hold s.Lock as documented; check gcSeries' check closure calls shouldEvict under series.Lock
The disabled-isolation fallback means no protection; the doc says it relies on callers not writing concurrently
